title: Karnataka heat intensifies amid rain deficit, temperatures rise up to 6°C above normal - NewsFirst Prime
full_text:
Several parts of Karnataka are witnessing unusually high temperatures, with North Interior Karnataka and coastal areas recording the sharpest rise.
Karnataka is experiencing a spell of unusual heat amid a shortage of monsoon rainfall, with temperatures climbing well above the normal levels across several parts of the state.
The rise is being felt not only during the day but also at night. While the maximum temperatures have increased, minimum temperatures have also moved up, leaving people with little relief even after sunset.
Several locations are recording temperatures 2 to 6°C higher than their usual levels. The heat is particularly noticeable in North Interior Karnataka and coastal districts, where temperatures have risen sharply.
Among the locations showing the biggest difference is Haveri, where the temperature has reached 34°C against a normal of 29°C, marking a rise of 6°C.

Dharwad has also recorded a significant increase, with the temperature touching 33°C compared to its normal of 29°C, which is 4°C above normal.
In Karwar, the temperature has climbed to 34°C, against the usual 31°C, a difference of 3.3°C. Honnavar has recorded 33°C, compared to its normal of 30°C, marking a 3°C rise.
In North Interior Karnataka, Kalaburagi has reached 35°C, against a normal temperature of 32°C, while Bidar has recorded 34°C compared to its usual 31°C. Both cities are therefore seeing temperatures 3°C above normal.
The heat is also being felt in other parts of the state. Chitradurga has recorded 33°C, against a normal of 29°C, making it 4°C higher than usual.
In Bengaluru, the temperature has risen to 30°C, compared to the normal 28°C, which is 2°C above normal.

Mysuru has recorded 32°C, against its normal temperature of 29°C, marking a 3°C increase.
The current conditions mean that residents are experiencing stronger heat during the daytime, while the rise in minimum temperatures is making nights warmer as well.
The temperature situation comes at a time when the state is already facing deficient monsoon conditions. With the expected rainfall not providing enough relief, the increase in temperatures has added to the discomfort across several districts.
The present figures show that the heat is not restricted to one region, with coastal Karnataka, North Interior Karnataka, Bengaluru, central areas and southern parts of the state all recording temperatures above their respective normal levels.
